nodes.label: Exactness Proves the Three Parts Are Not a Triangle
nodes.rationale: Exact closure forces treewidth one; a direct past–future constraint would force treewidth two; the two are incompatible, so the three parts are a path with the future reaching the past only through the present. Exactness and shape are the same fact read two ways.

nodes.label: Treewidth 1 ⟺ Exact Closure under ℛ
nodes.rationale: ℛ rebuilds a set from its pairwise projections and so enforces exactly pairwise consistency: a tree is made globally consistent by that alone (E = 0), while treewidth two needs strong 3-consistency and the shortfall shows as an envelope. Exhibited on the path {F ≤ Q ≤ P} at E = 0 against the triangle {|P−Q| ≤ F ≤ P+Q} at E > 0.

nodes.label: The Three-Body Case as a Genuine Triangle
nodes.rationale: The bracket's three parts do form a triangle, and there ℛ is exactly one consistency level short — which is why its surviving fraction falls as (1 − f)³ and why ℛ was never the right operator for it.
